step1_analysis.circuit_type: Differential Delay Cell for Ring Oscillator
step1_analysis.description: A differential amplifier with PMOS active loads, utilized as a delay stage in a ring oscillator for a 2.4-GHz frequency synthesizer. The PMOS loads are biased via RBIAS to control the resistance and thus the delay/frequency of the oscillator.

paper_reference.title: A 2.4-GHz Ring-Oscillator-Based CMOS Frequency Synthesizer With a Fractional Divider Dual-PLL Architecture

dc_power.description: DC power consumption of the delay cell

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming VBIAS=0.9V for high-speed operation: Vov = 0.9 - 0.42 = 0.48V. I_tail = 0.5 * 270uA/V^2 * (5/0.5) * (0.48V)^2 = 311 uA. Power = 1.8V * 311uA = 560 uW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Adjusted for SKY130 1.8V supply. A higher bias current is chosen to ensure sufficient bandwidth for 2.4 GHz oscillation.

sky130_expected.calculation: gm_n = 2 * 155uA / 0.48V = 645 uS. With RBIAS=0.9V, PMOS is in triode: R_on_p = 1 / (50uA/V^2 * 10 * (0.9 - 0.42)) = 4.1 kOhm. Gain = gm_n * R_on_p = 2.6 V/V = 8.3 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Ring oscillator delay cells require a moderate gain (typically 2-3 V/V) to sustain oscillation while maximizing bandwidth.

sky130_expected.calculation: BW = 1 / (2 * pi * R_on_p * C_load) = 1 / (2 * pi * 4.1kOhm * 10fF) = 3.8 GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The bandwidth of the individual delay cell must exceed the target oscillation frequency (2.4 GHz) to provide adequate phase shift.

phase_noise.description: Phase noise of the resulting ring oscillator

sky130_expected.calculation: N/A for a single open-loop cell.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends on the full closed-loop oscillator design, but SKY130 should achieve similar or better phase noise due to shorter channel lengths and faster transit times.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC power, AC differential gain, bandwidth, and transient output swing of the delay cell.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Differential Delay Cell Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u
.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm5=5u L_xm5=0.5u

XM4 VOUT_MINUS RBIAS N4 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}
XM1 VOUT_MINUS VIN_PLUS N3 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 VOUT_PLUS VIN_MINUS N3 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 N3 VBIAS GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM5 VOUT_PLUS RBIAS N4 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}

* Supply and Bias
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VN4 N4 VDD 0
VVBIAS VBIAS 0 0.9
VRBIAS RBIAS 0 0.9

* Differential Inputs
VVIN_PLUS VIN_PLUS 0 DC 0.9 AC 0.5 SIN(0.9 0.1 100MEG 0 0)
VVIN_MINUS VIN_MINUS 0 DC 0.9 AC -0.5 SIN(0.9 -0.1 100MEG 0 0)

* Load Capacitance
CL1 VOUT_PLUS 0 10f
CL2 VOUT_MINUS 0 10f

.control
* DC Analysis for Power
dc VVDD 1.8 1.8 1
let power = -i(VVDD) * 1.8
meas dc power_dc find power at=1.8
print power_dc

* AC Analysis for Gain and Bandwidth
ac dec 20 1k 100G
let vout_diff = v(VOUT_PLUS) - v(VOUT_MINUS)
let gain_db = 20 * log10(mag(vout_diff))
meas ac dc_gain find gain_db at=1k
let gain_3db = $&dc_gain - 3
meas ac bw when gain_db=gain_3db fall=1
print dc_gain bw

* Transient Analysis for Output Swing
tran 0.1n 50n
let vout_diff_tran = v(VOUT_PLUS) - v(VOUT_MINUS)
meas tran v_max max vout_diff_tran
meas tran v_min min vout_diff_tran
print v_max v_min

quit
.endc
.end
